title: Model arch perf notes: Llama / Mistral / Qwen (long-context, MoE routing)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for model-architecture-specific performance observations and open action items. Focus: Llama-family (70B-ish), Mistral (mix-size), Qwen (long-context), and MoE routing behavior for long-context workloads. We ran profiling across A100/80GB and RTX6000-ish nodes in our dedicated pools and synthetic long-context traces (up to 64k tokens) to capture kernel-level and runtime-level bottlenecks.

Summary of key findings (short):
- Long-context costs are dominated by attention kernel O(seq^2) and KV-cache memory management; for Qwen (designed for long context) we still see large memory-copy and synchronization overhead when seq > 8k.
- MoE routing overhead (top-k expert selection, scatter/gather, all-to-all) is a measurable fraction (~12-30%) of per-token latency at small batch sizes. Imbalance across experts causes spikes.
- Llama variants benefit strongly from fused attention (flash attention) and grouped GEMM kernels; when fused kernels are not used we see 25-40% slower token perf.
- Mistral shows competitive raw FLOPS efficiency for medium sequences, but memory-bound ops (KV, layernorm) limit gains when sequence grows.

Experimental setup (notes):
- Hardware: 1x NVIDIA A100 80GB (driver 525.x), 1x RTX6000 for comparison.
- Framework/runtime: Redwood serving-runtime v0.42 (local branch perf/prof-2026), CUDA 12, cuBLAS/cuDNN updated. Kernel selection layer enabled.
- Models: Llama-70B (float16), Mistral-7B-v0.3-ish (float16), Qwen-14B-mc (long-context variant), MoE-variant built on top of a 20B base (sparse experts=16, capacity=2x).
- Workloads: synthetic prompt shapes: short-chat (seq_in=64,gen=128), medium (seq_in=512,gen=256), long-context (seq_in=8192,gen=512), extreme (seq_in=32768,gen=128). Batches: 1, 4, 8.
- Profiling tools: nvprof/nsight for kernels, nvtx ranges instrumented in runtime, Triton logs, and custom per-token timing in infra.

Detailed observations:
1) Attention and KV-cache
- For seq<=512, attention compute dominates; flash attention fused kernels give ~1.3x speedup vs non-fused. For Llama-70B on A100: 1-token generation throughput (batch=1) improved from ~28 t/s -> ~38 t/s with fused attention. Numbers vary by context length.
- For seq>2048, memory copies (GPU-side memcpy for KV cache and repeated attention workspace allocations) start to dominate. In the 8k tests, memcpy+kernel-launch overheads contributed ~40-55% of the per-token latency. Root cause: our KV cache layout currently stores per-layer per-token tensors as distinct allocations (no large contiguous chunk), causing many small memcpy ops when serializing outputs or prepping for offload.
- Mitigation attempted: contiguous KV slab allocation reduced memcpy overhead by ~35% in long-context traces. Follow-up: convert per-layer KV to a single contiguous buffer per request and index view into it. See PR #987.

2) MoE routing overhead and imbalance
- Top-k gating and scatter/gather flow: measuring per-token cost, routing + pack/unpack ~12% of token latency at batch=8 for balanced synthetic load. At batch=1 this increases to ~28% because utility of batching experts is lower.
- Expert imbalance: under real prompts we observed up to 3x load on some experts vs median, causing tail-latency spikes due to straggler experts and retry/backpressure in our executor.
- All-to-all communication (when spanning multiple GPUs) incurs additional latency; in our multi-GPU tests, A2A cost added ~5-12ms per token depending on expert placement.
- Short-term mitigations tested: (a) local expert pinning to GPU when possible (reduced A2A), (b) soft capacity limit + fallback to dense FFN when overloaded (adds quality degradation but stabilizes latency). Results: soft capacity + fallback reduced 95th-p from 420ms -> 210ms on peak traces but had minor quality regressions on targeted prompts.

3) Kernel launch and small-batch inefficiency
- For small batch sizes and many short requests (PLG patterns), kernel launch overhead and host-to-device synchronization become significant. Observed per-launch latency ~30-50us for lightweight kernels; multiplied by thousands of small kernels per token (attention + FFN layers) this adds up.
- Approach: increase operator fusion (attention+bias+dropout, fused layernorm+FFN) using our custom CUDA kernels. Measured cumulative benefit of operator fusion ~20-30% for Llama/Mistral stacks at batch=1.

4) Quantization and reduced precision
- 4-bit quantization (PTQ) on Mistral gave ~1.8-2.2x throughput increase but worsened attention stability on long-context tests (occasional coherence issues). Qwen long-context version is sensitive to small rounding errors in rotary embeddings; need careful calibration.
- Mixed approach: keep attention in float16 and quantize FFN weights achieved most of the perf win while preserving generation quality. Action: expand quantization-aware evals for long-context.

5) Memory fragmentation and OOM patterns
- Long-context + large batch created fragmentation and several OOM events in A100 80GB due to multiple allocations from different components (runtime buffers + profiler traces + telemetry).
- Fixes: pre-reserve telemetry buffer pool behind a flag; adopt arena allocator for per-request temporary tensors. Early tests reduced fragmentation OOMs by ~90%.

Comparative throughput snapshot (single A100, batch=1, gen steady-state after warmup):
- Llama-70B float16 (seq_in=64,gen=128): ~38 tokens/sec (with fused attention)
- Mistral-7B float16 (seq_in=64,gen=128): ~160 tokens/sec
- Qwen-14B long-context (seq_in=8192,gen=256): ~6-12 tokens/sec (dominant attention cost + memcpy)
- MoE-20B sparse (16 experts, batch=1): effective throughput varies widely due to imbalance; median ~22 t/s, 95th ~8 t/s under skewed inputs
Notes: these are noisy synthetic numbers; absolute values depend on kernel selection, quant, and memory layout. Use for relative comparison only.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How to automatically balance experts at routing time without hurting quality? Need gating regularizers and dynamic load shedding heuristics; can we push gating computation to a fast fused kernel?
- Slotting vs contiguous KV: contiguous slab reduces memcpy but complicates incremental eviction/offload. Need design doc with tradeoffs for offload-friendly layout.
- A2A placement heuristics for MoE across multi-GPU nodes—best heuristic depends on prompt distribution; consider heuristic based on recent expert usage per tenant.
- Long-context quantization sensitivity: which operations must remain float16 for Qwen to maintain stability? We need automated per-op sensitivity tests.

Action items / next steps:
- [Maya] finish PR for contiguous KV-slab (PR #987) and add unit tests to simulate 8k–32k traces.
- [Aisha] expand MoE expert imbalance analysis with real customer traces (SRV-1423) and try gated regularizer variant in pilot branch.
- [Tom] implement arena allocator toggle and telemetry pool; validate no regressions in short-chat.
- [Diego] run a validation grid for mixed quant (attn float16, FFN 4-bit) across the Qwen family and log hallucination/regression metrics.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally informal; it contains open debug notes and rough numbers. If you see any numbers you'd like validated on more stable harness, flag them and assign an experiment ticket.
- Slack: #serving-runtime (thread: "moe-routing-spikes")

References / linked tickets:
- JIRA SRV-1423: customer-reported MoE tail latency
- PR 987: contiguous-KV-slab prototype
- Perf harness: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-perf (benchmark configs under /configs/long-context)

TODO / backlog ideas (low pri):
- Explore hybrid expert placement: colocate hot experts with tenant GPUs via cheap profiler and RL heuristic
- Consider kernel-assisted top-k gating: single CUDA kernel to compute gates + packed indices to reduce host round trips
- Probe using NVLINK P2P optimizations for A2A to lower all-to-all costs

End of notes.
